sections.h2: Which Clay County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three offices split the work in Clay County, Kentucky: the Property Valuation Administrator sets the assessed value, the Sheriff mails and collects the bill, and the County Clerk takes assessment appeals and holds unpaid bills after the sheriff's collection season ends. A seller who knows which door to knock on can clear up a tax question in one phone call instead of three.

All three work from the same address, 102 Richmond Road in Manchester, the county seat. The PVA does not set rates and does not collect money. Its job stops at the value on the roll.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Clay County itself?
sections.html:
Clay County covers 471 square miles of eastern Kentucky hill country, and Manchester is both the county seat and the largest city. The county was formed in 1807 from parts of Floyd, Knox and Madison counties, and a fire destroyed the courthouse in January 1936. It borders Owsley, Perry, Leslie, Bell, Knox, Laurel and Jackson counties and belongs to the Corbin micropolitan area.

The Census Bureau counted 20,345 residents in 2020 and estimated 19,465 for July 2025, a drop of 4.3 percent. That matters to a seller because the buyer pool is local and small. Census QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 give a clear picture of the housing stock:

  • 8,781 housing units and 7,288 households
  • 76.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $90,700
  • Median gross rent: $724 a month
  • Median owner costs: $978 with a mortgage and $367 without one

With values near $90,700, even a modest tax bill is a real share of a seller's net, so check the figure before you price the house.

sections.h2: How does the PVA value a house in Clay County?
sections.html:
The Clay County PVA values every parcel as of January 1 at fair cash value, meaning the price the property would bring in a voluntary sale between a willing buyer and a willing seller. The office also covers personal property. Public service companies, bank shares, omitted tangible property and vehicles are valued by the state Department of Revenue in Frankfort instead.

Each parcel must be physically inspected at least once every four years, and new construction goes onto the roll every year. If you bought in the prior year, the price on your deed can stand as the listed value for the next January 1, provided you changed nothing about the building. Owners list real estate between January 1 and March 1 only when the description on last year's roll is wrong or the property changed.

sections.h2: When are Clay County tax bills due?
sections.html:
Kentucky's standard collection season runs from early fall to mid-April, and the sheriff in Clay County collects within that frame. The Sheriff's page on the Fiscal Court site has a View Property Tax Bill button, so you can look up an amount by parcel. For the exact opening and closing dates the sheriff is using, call 606-598-3471, because the state allows 30-day phases when a different calendar is needed.

The state's typical sequence looks like this:

  • October 1 to November 1: pay with a 2 percent discount
  • November 2 to December 31: pay the face amount
  • January: a 5 percent penalty applies
  • February 1 to April 15: a 21 percent penalty applies

Property is assessed as of January 1, so a bill can arrive in a previous owner's name after a spring or summer sale.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Clay County assessment?
sections.html:
You must talk to the PVA before you can file anything. The steps run in a fixed order, and the filing window is short.

  • Watch for the assessment notice, which the PVA sends when a value goes up.
  • Book a conference with the PVA or a deputy during the tax roll inspection period, which opens the first Monday in May and runs Monday through Saturday for two weeks.
  • If you still disagree, file the appeal at the County Clerk's office by close of business on the next workday after inspection ends.
  • Appear before the local board of assessment appeals, which meets 25 to 35 days after inspection and sits no more than five days without state approval.
  • Bring evidence such as sales of similar houses, a recent appraisal or construction costs. A board must deny an appeal that arrives with no facts.

File and then fail to appear, and you lose the right to continue. A board decision can be taken further to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

sections.h2: Does Clay County offer a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes, for owners who are 65 or older or who are classified as totally disabled and who live in the home. The exemption for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years is $49,100, subtracted from the assessed value before tax is figured. A home valued at the county's $90,700 median would be taxed on $41,600.

You apply at the PVA office in Manchester at 606-598-3832, with a driver's license, birth certificate or passport as proof of age. Disability claims need documentation of the federal or retirement-system classification. Some disabled owners must reapply each year, while veterans with a service-connected disability and people deemed permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems do not.

sections.h2: What happens if a Clay County tax bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
At the close of business on April 15, the unpaid bill moves from the sheriff to the County Clerk and becomes a certificate of delinquency, which is a lien on the property. Interest of 1 percent a month starts running, and a 10 percent clerk fee and a 20 percent county attorney fee are added.

The county attorney sends notices in May and, if needed, June, and may agree to an installment plan. Beginning in mid-July the clerk can offer certificates to outside buyers, with sales running into late October. Once an investor buys the certificate, you deal with that buyer, and more fees pile on. The Clay County Clerk's website keeps a delinquent tax page for each year.

sections.h2: How are taxes handled when I sell a house in Clay County?
sections.html:
The title or closing agent normally pays the current bill from your proceeds and prorates it between you and the buyer. Any open delinquency has to be cleared first, since the lien follows the parcel. Ask the sheriff for a payoff figure before you sign a contract, and ask the PVA whether an exemption on the parcel will end with the sale.

On the deed itself, Kentucky charges the seller a transfer tax of fifty cents for each $500 of value or fraction, collected by the County Clerk when the deed is recorded. On a $90,700 sale that comes to $91. Deeds that only correct an earlier deed, transfers between spouses in a divorce, foreclosure deeds and nominal-value transfers between parent and child are exempt.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Clay County?
faqs.a: The Clay County Sheriff sends and collects it. Call 606-598-3471 or use the View Property Tax Bill button on the sheriff's page of the Fiscal Court site if a bill never arrives.

faqs.q: Can I still dispute my Clay County assessment after the May inspection period?
faqs.a: Generally no. The conference and the clerk filing both have to happen inside the inspection window, with the filing due by the next workday after it closes. Call the PVA at 606-598-3832 in the spring to book a conference.

faqs.q: Does the PVA collect any money in Clay County?
faqs.a: No. The PVA only values property and handles exemptions. Payment goes to the sheriff, and after mid-April to the County Clerk.

faqs.q: Do I pay transfer tax when I sell my Clay County house?
faqs.a: Yes, in most sales. The seller owes fifty cents per $500 of value, and the clerk collects it before recording the deed. Exempt transfers include foreclosure deeds, divorce transfers and deeds that correct an earlier deed.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Clay County house that has a delinquent tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes, but the delinquency must be paid at or before closing. Ask the County Clerk for the amount with interest and fees so the title company can include it in the payoff.
